The *Sīhakotthujātaka* (Ja 188) is a story of the Pali *Jātaka* collection, translated under the title *The Lion-Jackal* [SuttaCentral]. According to the narrative framework preserved in its opening blurb, the story was delivered by the Buddha while residing at Jetavana with reference to the monk Kokālika, opening with the verse line: "Lion’s claws and lion’s paws" [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records four translations of the text in four modern languages [SuttaCentral].

No curated cross-canonical parallels are identified on SuttaCentral, and no Pali-internal text reuse is reported [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
